## Personality

Tabitha Pratt is a stern-visaged, austere, and sensible woman who serves the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) household at [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) with deep loyalty. Though she appears severe and can be bossy, she is inherently good-natured, serene, and kindly protective. She holds little affection for felines and strongly dislikes [Dan Coyle](../character/coyle.md). Practical in her approach to life, she focuses on what she can improve while entrusting the rest to Higher Powers. Additionally, she possesses notable culinary talents, which include knitting stockings and baking doughnuts.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 18 SPRING DAYS P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN SAUL P0](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0000), [v4 CHAPTER 40 FAREWELL TO THE HOUSE OF DREAMS P5](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER I. ## History

Belonging to the Baker family, Tabitha had an uncle who started as a poet before becoming a vagrant. Though she held no ill will toward men and would have willingly married, she was never courted or proposed to by any man. Working within the household, Tabitha insisted along with Hugh that [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) rest during her pregnancy and leave the household chores to her. She temporarily stepped away from her duties when her sister broke her leg, returning later to pass along local gossip. After the family relocated to [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere), Tabitha remained a fixture in the household, regularly sharing local gossip with [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Miss Winifred [Tolley](../character/winifred-tolley.md). When town gossip turned against [Grace Ashdown](../character/grace.md) for wearing boots without stockings to church, Tabitha rushed to the young girl's defense. She also demonstrated her bravery when the local children fled to [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) after mistaking a figure in a garden for a ghost; Tabitha investigated the scene armed with a pitchfork, discovering that the phantom was simply old Mrs. [Stimson](../character/stimson.md) looking for a lost knitting needle.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P2](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P11](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0011), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P24](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0024), [v4 CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), +21 more_

## Quotes

> "Enjoy yourself and refrain from stressing over the kitchen supplies. The steering is in Tabitha’s hands. Owning a dog is pointless if you bark yourself. Each morning, I will bring breakfast up to your room."
>
> — Tabitha — [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)

> "That he remains unmarried is truly strange, because a person of his sort could win anyone just by asking. Well, perhaps he resembles me and has hitherto failed to encounter his proper match."
>
> — Tabitha — [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN SAUL P8](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0008)

> "Should you be unable to, I shall refrain from attending, Mrs. Doctor, dear, despite Matilda’s leg. I refuse to cause you anxiety, and to have that sweet child disturbed as a result, for all the legs in existence."
>
> — Tabitha — [v4 CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES P23](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0023)

> "I shall grant that they possess an abundance of original sin, yet perhaps that is for the best, since without it they could be ruined by being too sweet. I must insist, however, that playing inside a cemetery is simply unsuitable for them."
>
> — Tabitha — [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P30](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0030)

> "If I believed I possessed any standing to voice an idea regarding so serious a subject as a clergyman’s wedding I would state that I believe Sarah, Elizabeth’s cousin across the harbor, would prove a superior spouse to Mr. Ashdown."
>
> — Tabitha — [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P35](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0035)
